name: Stuffed Grape Leaves
author: armenianmuseum.org
steps: Wash rice in cold water until water runs clear.
Sauté onions in olive oil until tender.
Add spices and stir until fragrant.
Bring to a gentle boil, then simmer for 30 minutes until all stock is absorbed and rice is tender.
Serve as a side dish or filling for dolmas.

culture.text: Stuffed leaves—more commonly known by its sub-types stuffed grape leaves, stuffed vine leaves, or stuffed cabbage leaves—are a food made of leaves rolled around a filling of minced meat, grains such as rice, or both. It is occasionally known in the English-speaking world by its Turkish name, sarma, which, as a dish of the Ottoman Empire, is also used in Armenian and some Eastern European languages. Since the Ottoman Empire's dissolution, its popularity persists in Turkish, Bulgarian, Persian, Greek, Romanian, Iraqi, Levantine, Egyptian, former Yugoslav constituent states, and Armenian cuisines.
